prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Mina Castellan for the job below.

About the freelancer: 5 years experience; skills: SQL, Excel, Power BI, Google Sheets, data analysis, dashboard, data cleaning, data visualization

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Build a database of golf courses across America.
I'm looking for help building a database of remote golf courses that are between 30 - 130 miles away from major southern cities in the US including the following and in this order of interest: - Dallas - Houston - Austin - Atlanta - Tampa - Los Angeles - Charlotte - Jacksonville - Miami - Orlando - Tallahhassee - Nashville - Phoenix - Denver - Salt Lake City The goal of the exercise is to find a few courses that are great candidates for acquisition and transforming them into a new experiential golf brand. Here's the Google spreadsheet we'll share access to: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1g6XxPCirzABigpjzUD4yJpYjdmJ5ggUo_HWrSm53NtM/edit?usp=sharing The inputs on the spreadsheet are as follows: - Course Name - City - State - Address - Closest Big City - Distance from Big City - Owner - Owner Contact Info (email and / or phone number) All I'm looking for is a comprehensive list with all inputs filled out for each course that's added.
</job>

text:
I’m passionate, hard-working, and I’d love to help build this golf course database for you.

I have 5 years of experience working with SQL, Excel, Power BI, Google Sheets, data analysis, dashboarding, data cleaning, and data visualization, and I’m comfortable turning messy or incomplete data into a clean, usable spreadsheet. For this project, I’d focus on building a comprehensive list that follows your required fields exactly: Course Name, City, State, Address, Closest Big City, Distance from Big City, Owner, and Owner Contact Info. I understand the importance of accuracy here, especially since the goal is to identify strong acquisition candidates and not just create a basic directory.

A couple of relevant projects I’ve worked on:
- For Juniper & Ash Home, I built Shopify customer segments from order exports using recency, frequency, and spend, and the top segment represented 9% of customers and 41% of revenue.
- For a manufacturing client, I built an HR attrition and absence dashboard in Power BI, Excel, and SQL, and it covered 1,900 employees.

Those projects reflect the same strengths I’d bring to this job: careful data gathering, structured organization, and a focus on creating something decision-ready. I’m also comfortable working in Google Sheets and keeping information consistent across many rows, which will matter a lot when you’re evaluating courses by geography, ownership, and distance from major cities.

I’d approach this by systematically researching each target metro area in your order of interest, identifying courses that fall within the 30–130 mile range, and filling in each field as completely as possible. I can also help keep the spreadsheet clean and easy to review so you can quickly compare opportunities across cities.

If you’d like, I can get started right away and work through the spreadsheet in a structured way.
